args.title: Parse the header line with splitFields so quoted column names are recognised
args.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

parseStatement splits the header line with a plain `lines[0].split(",")` instead of the quote-aware `splitFields` used for data rows. When a statement's header is double-quoted (e.g. `"Date","Amount","Description","Reference"`), the resulting column names keep their quotes (`"date"` instead of `date`), so none of REQUIRED_COLUMNS match and assertShape throws "errors.rowShape" at row 1. Use `splitFields(lines[0])` (lower-cased) to build the header, matching how data rows are parsed.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

parseStatement parses the header line with a plain `lines[0].split(",")`, unlike data rows, which go through the quote-aware `splitFields`. When the header is fully double-quoted, the column names keep their quote characters (`"date"` instead of `date`), so none match REQUIRED_COLUMNS and the row-shape check throws at row 1 even though the file is well-formed. Data rows pass because they already use `splitFields`. The fix is to run the header line through `splitFields` as well.
